headline: Continued 500 Easthampton Road hearing and 5 Appleton Street enforcement order; closed 233 Easthampton Road order.
summary: A representative for the 500 Easthampton Road project said the remaining endangered species review could take a month or more. Topsoil, fencing and plantings were installed at 233 Easthampton Road, and the site will be inspected after the next two growing seasons. Staff said the panel picked Sean Mullen as Conservation Planner, with a tentative start date of September 28th.
decisions: Continued the public hearing for 500 Easthampton Road to the October 8th meeting, 7-0.
Closed the enforcement order for 233 Easthampton Road, with inspections after the 2026 and 2027 growing seasons, 7-0.
Continued the enforcement order for 5 Appleton Street to the September 24th meeting, 7-0.

Vice Chairperson Moriarty made a motion to close out the enforcement order for 233 Easthampton Road, with the plan that the Commission inspect the restoration after the 2026 growing season and again after the 2027 growing season... Commissioner Normand seconded the motion, which was approved unanimously, 7-0.

Vice Chairperson Moriarty made a motion to continue the order to an upcoming September 24th meeting, reminding the responsible party to follow on their promises for erosion control, the silt fence and NHESP application. Commissioner Arnold seconded the motion, which was approved unanimously, 7-0.
Commissioner Arnold made a motion to cancel the September 10th Conservation Commission meeting. Commissioner Normand seconded the motion, which was approved unanimously, 6-0.

Holyoke Conservation Commission Meeting 
Minutes 8/27/26  
Conservation Commission Members Present: Jeffery Horan (Chairperson), Mary Moriarty (Vice Chairperson), 
Patricia Normand, John Perdrizet, Bernice Bowler, Rosemary Arnold, Michael Dodge 
Conservation Commission Members Absent: None 
Staff Present: Maggie Herlihy (Conservation Planner) 
Members of the Public Present: Peter Rosskothen, John Furman, Nathan Moyer 
 
1. Call to Order 
Chairperson Horan called the meeting to order at 6:20 p.m.  
 
2. Public Hearing – Notice of Intent DEP WE# 186-0306 – Continued from 3/26/26 
Applicant: Salmar Realty, Inc. 
Representative: R. Levesque Associates 
Location: 500 Easthampton Road (MBP: 213-00-003, 212-00-001) 
Description: Commercial redevelopment within the Buffer Zone of Bordering Vegetated Wetlands 
 
Chairperson Horan invited Peter Rosskothen to speak on behalf of the project.  He provided an update on the 
remaining Natural Heritage & Endangered Species review.  He explained that litigation concerning the City 
permitting for the property had concluded during the prior year and that the primary remaining issue involved 
mitigation associated with historic work at the Log Cabin.  He stated that the, around 1999 or 2000, the Log Cabin 
addition had not gone through the proper endangered-species permitting process and that Natural Heritage was 
therefore considering the historic impacts together with the proposed development on the property in front of the 
Log Cabin.  Approximately 8.2 acres behind the Log Cabin had been acquired for potential permanent protection, 
and the parties were working with Natural Heritage to determine the amount of land required for mitigation.  Mr. 
Rosskothen stated that the parties had generally agreed on the amount of land needed and that the City of 
Easthampton was willing to accept and permanently protect a portion of the property. He estimated that the 
remaining work could take another month or more. 
 
Commissioner Arnold noted that a small chunk of land is to be taken off Edna Williams to help the Log Cabin and 
asked for clarification on that situation.  Mr. Rosskothen commented on what he knew of the situation and 
expressed that he thinks it's great for the Log Cabin. 
 
Ms. Herlihy shared a diagram of the ANR (Approval Not Required) which showed the Edna Williams parcel.  She 
explained that it contains land both in Holyoke but also some in Easthampton that the City of Holyoke owns, and 
that they have to go before both the Easthampton and Holyoke Planning Boards before taking it to Holyoke City 
Council.  Under the plan, approximately 0.36 acres would remain City of Holyoke property temporarily before 
being sold to the Log Cabin, and an approximately 1.59-acre portion would also be proposed for sale to the Log 
Cabin after Holyoke Planning Board and City Council review.
Page 2 of 5 
 
Commissioner Arnold asked whether the proposed property divisions would affect Mr. Rosskothen's abutting 
property.  Mr. Rosskothen stated that the portion adjoining his property was largely wetland and did not appear to 
provide commercially usable land for his project. He noted that the transaction would, however, be valuable to the 
Log Cabin by resolving an existing shed/easement issue and providing usable land near the upper portion of the 
property. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty asked whether the requested continuance satisfied the parameter that work was being 
done with Natural Heritage.  Ms. Herlihy affirmed that this was the case, reviewing the applicable 310 CMR 
language and correspondence supplied by the project team showing continued communications with Natural 
Heritage.  Based on that documentation, she stated that the project continued to show progress and that she did 
not believe there were grounds to require a new filing. 
 
After discussing the expected timeframe of the project, the Commission determined that a six-week continuance 
was more realistic than returning at the next meeting.  Commissioner Bernice Bowler made a motion to continue 
the public hearing for 500 Easthampton Road to the October 8th meeting.  Commissioner Normand second the 
motion, which was approved unanimously, 7-0. 
 
3. Enforcement Order – Continued from 6/25/26 
Location: 233 Easthampton Road (MBP: 141-00-002) 
Description: Soil grading, mounding and rutting from heavy equipment usage across approximately 25,000 square 
feet of undeveloped land within the 100 foot Buffer Zone of Banks and Bordering Vegetated Wetlands. 
 
Chairperson Horan invited John Furman to provide an update on the project.  Mr. Furman reported that topsoil had 
been installed by Geeleher Enterprises, the protective fence had been completed by Cesar, and a landscaping 
company hired by Geeleher installed the required landscape plantings.  The landscaper used additional topsoil in 
the planting holes to avoid placing the new vegetation directly into gravel.  They have been watering the plants. 
 
Mr. Furman shared an image of the previously-approved mitigation plan, as well as recent photographs depicting 
progress that has been made which depicted fences, gates and growing plants.  He explained that periodic stops 
will be made to the site to ensure that plants are growing as intended.  The Commission expressed their pleasure 
with how the project is coming along. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty asked how many growing seasons the site will have to be monitored for and whose 
responsibility that would be.  Ms. Herlihy answered and reported that she and Mr. Pellegrino had also inspected 
the property recently, being generally pleased with what they observed.  She suggested that the erosion controls 
could possibly be removed since they aren't in great shape anyway.  She also expressed the Commission's approval 
of the language for maintenance and success.  She suggested closing the enforcement order with a later date 
chosen for future review.  
 
Commissioner Perdrizet inquired about the ability to replant dead plants on the site, and Ms. Herlihy added a 
question about whether the plants have a warranty.  Mr. Furman explained that the plants were not covered by a 
landscaper warranty because watering responsibility would shift to the property owner, but he and the project 
team would continue monitoring the site and would require replacement of clearly failed plantings as needed to 
meet the approved success standard.  Chairperson Horan stated that the Commission should inspect the property 
after the current growing season and again after the next growing season to verify establishment.  Commissioner
Page 3 of 5 
 
Normand asked about the possibility of deer destroying the plants, citing another case where that had occurred.  
Mr. Furman acknowledged it as a valid concern and said he'll recommend fencing if it becomes apparent that deer 
will be a problem. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty made a motion to close out the enforcement order for 233 Easthampton Road, with the 
plan that the Commission inspect the restoration after the 2026 growing season and again after the 2027 growing 
season, and for the erosion controls to be removed between September 15th and October 15th, 2026.  
Commissioner Normand seconded the motion, which was approved unanimously, 7-0. 
 
4. Enforcement Order – Continued from 8/13/26 
Location: 5 Appleton Street (MBP: 049-01-006) 
 
Description: Grading and fill deposition along approximately 470 lineal feet of banks within Riverfront, Banks, and 
Priority and Estimated Habitats of Rare Species associated with the Connecticut River. Fill sediments and 
associated debris were observed eroding down the steep bank towards the water. 
 
No project representative attended the meeting.  Ms. Herlihy reported that the representatives had requested a 
continuance.  Ms. Herlihy reported that VHB representative Sara Berryman had not yet submitted the Natural 
Heritage review but expected to do so shortly, and Randy Reynolds had not yet received a response from Pinsly 
Railroad.  Ms. Herlihy informed that she had revisited the property to check the erosion controls that the 
Commission had previously directed the applicant to repair, sharing photos, and it didn't appear that they had 
been fixed.  There didn't appear to be any new site activity.  Vice Chairperson Moriarty mentioned that erosion 
control fencing was to be put up a little higher near the building, but Ms. Herlihy didn't observe that any such 
fencing had been built. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty made a motion to continue the order to an upcoming September 24th meeting, 
reminding the responsible party to follow on their promises for erosion control, the silt fence and NHESP 
application.  Commissioner Arnold seconded the motion, which was approved unanimously, 7-0.  
 
5. Discussion – MassDEP Engagement 
Staff updated the Commission following the retirement of longtime MassDEP Western Region Circuit Rider Mark 
Stinson.  Ms. Herlihy reported that MassDEP had posted the vacant position and that another circuit rider was 
available as an interim contact while the hiring process proceeded. 
Ms. Herlihy mentioned a webinar from the previous year hosted by MassDEP inviting Western Region conservation 
commissions, and that most attendees from more rural commissions were noted to have different problems than 
those of Holyoke.  She suggested that this MassDEP follow-up opportunity was a chance to engage with the 
Holyoke Conservation Commission's problems more specifically.  She pointed out a link to a feedback form for 
individual commissioners to fill out.  The Commission discussed various engagement topics that might be 
suggested, such as wetlands delineation review.  Ms. Herlihy mentioned that MassDEP in the past has offered to 
come out and speak to commissions about specific topics and that such a thing may be worth requesting once the 
Circuit Rider position is filled. 
The Commission noted a member of the public named Nathan in attendance, who stated he was just there to listen 
and learn how the Commission's meetings go since he has a conservation background.  Commissioner Arnold 
welcomed him saying that more younger people interested in the Conservation Commission are needed.
Page 4 of 5 
 
6. Discussion – Updates regarding the Conservation Planner and City Forester positions 
Chairperson Horan reported that four interviews of applications had recently been completed after receieving 22 
applications.  The interview panel consisted of Chairperson Horan, Ms. Herlihy and Mr. Pellegrino.  The panel 
selected Sean Mullen for the position of Conservation Planner.  His tentative start date was set for September 28th, 
after a previously-scheduled vacation.  
 
The Commission also discussed the new City Forester, Nate Morrell, whose start date was expected later in 
September after a vacation.  Chairperson Horan noted that Mr. Pellegrino, Mr. Mullen and Mr. Morrell had 
overlapping professional connections through Greening the Gateway Cities and shared mentors.  He expressed 
confidence that the new staff would work well together.  Ms. Herlihy described Mr. Pellegrino as a quick learner 
who was already taking responsibility for department tasks and stated that Mr. Mullen had demonstrated initiative 
by attending a Commission meeting and spending time in the office learning the role before his formal start date. 
 
Vice Chairperson Moriarty raised the possibility of alternate or associate members who could attend regularly, 
learn the Commission's work, and potentially fill in when a quorum issue.  Chairperson Horan mentioned past 
discussion about that possibly, though he noted that associate members would be non-voters.  Ms. Herlihy noted 
that other conservation commissions in Massachusetts use alternate members who can sit in for a voting member 
in certain circumstances such as an issue with quorum.  Commissioners also discussed outreach to qualified 
applicants from the recent planner search and the importance of seeking a broader and more diverse pool of future 
participants.    
 
7. Discussion – Going away luncheon for Maggie Herlihy 
The Commission confirmed plans for Ms. Herlihy's farewell luncheon on Wednesday, September 2nd.  Members 
discussed attendance and advance meal orders and agreed that Joey Pellegrino, Sean Mullen, and Yoni Glogower 
should be invited so the gathering could include both departing and incoming members of the conservation team.  
Ms. Herlihy stated that she would contact Yoni regarding the invitation.  Commissioners thanked Ms. Herlihy for 
her service and work with the Commission. 
 
8. Formal Vote – Minutes from 5/14/26 Meeting 
Ms. Herlihy reported that InfraWare had completed draft minutes for May 14, May 28, and June 11, with the May 
14 draft being the first she had fully reviewed and edited.  She stated that the external service was providing a 
quick turnaround but that Commissioners had expressed a preference for more detailed minutes.  The Commission 
discussed that Sean Mullen may be preparing meeting minutes as part of his Conservation Planner responsibilities 
in the future. 
 
Ms. Herlihy also noted Vice Chairperson Moriarty's prior feedback that the minutes should use “moved” as the verb 
and “motion” as the noun.  Commissioner Bowler identified wording in the May 14 draft referring to earlier 
minutes as being “enclosed,” and Ms. Herlihy agreed to review and remove that language if it remained in the final 
version.  Ms. Herlihy informed that the May 28 and June 11 minutes would be placed in the Commission's Google 
Drive minutes folder for review. 
 
9. Discussion – Upcoming Items for 9/10/26 Meeting 
Ms. Herlihy noted that almost nothing is on the agenda for the upcoming meeting.  She mentioned that the Holyoke 
Gas & Electric yearly operations plan in the final version had been received.  The Commission had been contacted
Page 5 of 5 
 
earlier in the year to provide comments for the draft version.  Because there were no other significant items 
expected for the September 10th meeting agenda, it could be moved to the following meeting instead if the meeting 
on the 10th is to be cancelled. 
 
Commissioner Arnold made a motion to cancel the September 10th Conservation Commission meeting. 
Commissioner Normand seconded the motion, which was approved unanimously, 6-0.  Michael Dodge was no 
longer present for the vote.   
 
10. Mail/other items not reasonably anticipated by the Chair 
Commissioner Perdrizet suggested considering a hands-on volunteer or community group that could assist with 
visible conservation work such as helping newly planted trees survive, supporting tree planting, or periodically 
observing conservation sites, possibly providing a bridge to becoming a member of the Conservation Commission 
eventually. 
 
Chairperson Horan noted that an urban forestry committee had been discussed in the past but had raised 
questions about staff capacity and responsibility.  He informed that the Mayor had considered it in the past, and 
City Council had put in an order for it that never yielded any results.  He suggested that they may talk about the 
possibility more down the road, but that ought to be after they have more information on the plan they will put 
forth to the Mayor.  Ms. Herlihy said that they may have a better timeline for the plan after speaking with the Mayor 
the following Wednesday.  Chairperson Horan noted how well the last meeting with the Mayor was, as the Mayor 
showed pleasure with the Commission's work and agenda. 
 
11. Adjourn 
Commissioner Bowler made a motion to adjourn at 7:56 p.m., and the meeting was subsequently ended.
